clean_source_blocks.text: The 14-paragraph memo includes an end to fighting, an agreement that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and a $300bn redevelopment package for Iran.

A US-Iran agreement to extend the ceasefire between the two countries has been signed and is now in effect, a White House official has confirmed to the BBC. President Donald Trump formally signed the deal - which is set to reopen the pivotal Strait of Hormuz - while attending the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains in France. The 14-point agreement, which is known as a Memorandum of Understanding, says that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and also commits a $300 billion fund for the "reconstruction and economic development" of the country - although the US is not required to contribute. It comes four months after the conflict between the countries - and Israel - broke out. The agreement has been described by the Trump administration as "performance-based", with Iran benefitting only if it complies with its commitments.

It comes four months after the conflict between the countries - and Israel - broke out.

The agreement has been described by the Trump administration as "performance-based", with Iran benefitting only if it complies with its commitments. While the text of the deal leaves many questions unanswered - and many key issues unsolved - here's what we know about some of the key points. Initial US-Iran agreement leaves many key issues to be negotiated The first paragraph of the agreement notes that the US, Iran and allies will declare an "immediate and permanent" termination of military operations on "all fronts" - including Lebanon. From the US perspective, Trump has been growing increasingly concerned that Israeli military operations against Hezbollah could upend the agreement with Iran. Tehran, for its part, has repeatedly said it expected Lebanon to be covered by the truce.

A US-Iran agreement to extend the ceasefire between the two countries has been signed and is now in effect, a White House official has confirmed to the BBC.

President Donald Trump formally signed the deal - which is set to reopen the pivotal Strait of Hormuz - while attending the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains in France.

The 14-point agreement, which is known as a Memorandum of Understanding, says that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and also commits a $300 billion fund for the "reconstruction and economic development" of the country - although the US is not required to contribute. It comes four months after the conflict between the countries - and Israel - broke out.

The agreement has been described by the Trump administration as "performance-based", with Iran benefitting only if it complies with its commitments.

While the text of the deal leaves many questions unanswered - and many key issues unsolved - here's what we know about some of the key points.

The first paragraph of the agreement notes that the US, Iran and allies will declare an "immediate and permanent" termination of military operations on "all fronts" - including Lebanon.

From the US perspective, Trump has been growing increasingly concerned that Israeli military operations against Hezbollah could upend the agreement with Iran.

Tehran, for its part, has repeatedly said it expected Lebanon to be covered by the truce.

Any continuation of Israeli military operations in Lebanon would constitute a "violation of the understanding" and "necessary measures will be taken", a spokesperson for the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Wednesday.

The agreement notes that "from now on" neither side will initiate military operations or threaten each other, and ensure "the territorial integrity and sovereignty" of Lebanon.

The final agreement will lead to the permanent "termination" of the conflict, the document says.

It is unclear how Israel will react to this point.

WASHINGTON/TEHRAN - President Donald Trump signed an interim deal to end the war with Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, speeding up the timeline for the agreement to go into effect despite blowback from Republicans who said it amounted to a victory for Tehran.

The so-called memorandum of understanding is now in effect, a US official said. It was unclear if Iran had immediately begun taking steps to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump told reporters he signed the document at the palace of Versailles near Paris, where he had dinner with French President Emmanuel Macron. Versailles was where leaders of the great powers gathered in 1919 to sign the peace treaty that formally ended World War I.

The memorandum had been signed digitally on June 14 by Vice-President J.D. Vance and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghali...

payload.title: Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin tulitaukosopimus tuli voimaan
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin sopimus tulitauon jatkamisesta on allekirjoitettu ja tullut voimaan. Sopimukseen sisältyy sotatoimien lopettaminen, Iranin ydinaseettomuutta koskeva kirjaus sekä 300 miljardin dollarin jälleenrakennus- ja kehitysrahasto.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin sopimus tulitauon jatkamisesta on allekirjoitettu ja tullut voimaan, Valkoisen talon virkamies on vahvistanut BBC:lle. Presidentti Donald Trump allekirjoitti yhteisymmärryspöytäkirjana kuvatun 14-kohtaisen sopimuksen G7-kokouksen yhteydessä Ranskan Evian-les-Bainsissa, ja järjestelyn on määrä avata uudelleen strategisesti tärkeäksi kuvattu Hormuzinsalmi.

## Sopimus lopettaa sotatoimet

Sopimuksen ensimmäisessä kohdassa Yhdysvaltojen, Iranin ja liittolaisten on määrä julistaa sotilaallisten operaatioiden välitön ja pysyvä päättäminen kaikilla rintamilla. Kirjauksen kerrotaan kattavan myös Libanonin. Sopimus tulee voimaan neljä kuukautta sen jälkeen, kun konflikti Yhdysvaltojen, Iranin ja Israelin välillä puhkesi.

Yhdysvaltain näkökulmasta yhtenä huolena on ollut se, että Israelin sotilasoperaatiot Hizbollahia vastaan voisivat horjuttaa Iranin kanssa tehtyä järjestelyä. Teheran on puolestaan toistuvasti sanonut odottaneensa, että Libanon sisällytetään tulitaukoon. Tämä tekee Libanonia koskevasta kirjauksesta yhden sopimuksen keskeisistä kohdista, vaikka teksti jättää lähdeaineiston mukaan useita kysymyksiä avoimiksi.

## Ydinasekirjaus ja kehitysrahasto

Sopimuksessa todetaan, ettei Iranilla koskaan ole ydinaseita. Lisäksi siihen sisältyy 300 miljardin dollarin rahasto maan jälleenrakennukseen ja taloudelliseen kehitykseen. Yhdysvaltojen ei kuitenkaan kerrota olevan velvoitettu osallistumaan rahaston rahoittamiseen, joten rahaston käytännön toteutus jää lähdeaineiston perusteella avoimeksi.

Trumpin hallinto on kuvannut järjestelyä suoritusperusteiseksi. Tämä tarkoittaa, että Iran hyötyisi sopimuksesta vain, jos se noudattaa omia sitoumuksiaan. Sopimuksen vaikutukset riippuvat siten siitä, miten osapuolet toteuttavat pöytäkirjaan kirjatut kohdat ja miten vielä ratkaisematta olevat kysymykset käsitellään jatkoneuvotteluissa.

## Neuvottelut jatkuvat

Lähdeaineiston mukaan alustava Yhdysvaltain ja Iranin välinen sopimus jättää monia keskeisiä asioita neuvoteltavaksi myöhemmin. Vaikka tulitauon jatkaminen, Hormuzinsalmen avaaminen, ydinasekirjaus ja kehitysrahasto on kirjattu sopimukseen, tekstin kaikkia käytännön seurauksia ei ole vielä ratkaistu.
